trees.note: Opened by the ask-outing rule. While the follower is waiting for an answer this REPLACES the everyday Talk-to script, so walking over and talking to it is how you answer - no magic word typed into public chat, and no follower listening to the whole street. The node carrying "answer" is what feeds the reply back to the rules: yes puts a want on the board, no closes it politely.

says: I wanted to ask you something, and I'd rather ask it properly.
Have you got time to go somewhere with me? Nowhere far. Just somewhere I like.
We go where you need to go. That's the arrangement, and no complaints from me.
But there are places I'd go if it were up to me, and it never is.

you: All right. Where did you have in mind?

says: Give me a moment. I'll think of somewhere.

trees.note: A game, opened by the offer-game rule the same way want-outing is opened by ask-outing. The reveal is deliberately NOT in here: a tree is fixed text, so a guess it resolved itself would have the same answer every time. The box closes on "hold on", and the verdict arrives overhead a beat later from game-hands-won and game-hands-lost, which split a coin flip between them by priority. That also puts the reveal where the follower is standing rather than in a menu, which is where a reveal belongs.

says: Both hands behind my back. One of them's got something in it.

choices.label: What have you got in there?

you: What have you got in there?

says: Left. You sound sure. Hold on.
Fair enough. They'll both still be here later.
